summary: Step 8 (ARCHITECTURE) DONE - Architecture Bootstrap Reconciliation. All eight approved corrections are implemented. (1) NO rule-ID duplication: ArchitectureBootstrap receives the canonical ArchitectureVersion through an injected factory, so the bootstrap module contains no rule identifiers at all (a guard test asserts that none of ARCHITECTURE_V1.rule_ids() appears in its source) and does not import the architecture layer (also guarded); the bootstrap imports only domain, ports, stdlib and its sibling application managers. The composition side - tests today, a composition root later - derives the spec from ARCHITECTURE_V1 (version, description, rule_ids) and injects it. (2) Idempotence is reconciliation, not 'skip if exists': each item resolves to created, already-present (semantically identical) or a raised BootstrapConflictError. Nothing is ever silently overwritten - a differing ArchitectureVersion conflicts instead of being replaced, an already-current different version conflicts instead of rewriting history, and a conflicting ADR or Risk is never amended. (3) Project handling: created only when absent; when it already exists its live runtime state is left completely untouched (a test seeds mode=AUTO, paused=True, snapshot=5, plan_version=0.2 and asserts all four survive); a differently named project or more than one project is an explicit conflict rather than a silent singleton violation. (4) ADR/Risk reconciliation compares content AND status (ADR must be ACCEPTED, Risk must be OPEN); every retrospective ADR carries the provenance note 'Decision established during implementation Steps 1-7 and formally recorded during Architecture Bootstrap Reconciliation.' Both spec and seeded rows are asserted to carry it. (5) BootstrapSummary explicitly distinguishes created from already-present per item, and conflicts are raised as BootstrapConflictError carrying the conflict descriptions - seed() never partially commits because the whole reconciliation runs inside one storage.transaction() (the managers' own transactions nest and join it per Step 5). (6) All Risk severity/impact values come from the existing Step 1 Severity enum (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL) and all statuses from RiskStatus/ADRStatus/Mode; no new enum value was introduced, and a test asserts the specs only use existing enum values. (7) All mandated tests exist: a second identical seed creates 0 records and writes 0 audit events; an existing ArchitectureVersion with different rules conflicts and rolls everything back; another current ArchitectureVersion conflicts and leaves history untouched; an existing ADR with the same id but a different decision conflicts; an existing Risk with the same id but a different mitigation conflicts; an existing Project is never reset to MANUAL; and the canonical version is injected rather than hard-coded. Two additional rollback tests prove no partial commit by parking the conflict on the LAST risk and asserting that the project, baseline, all seven ADRs and the nineteen audit entries vanished. (8) Rest as approved. Deliverable content: 7 retrospective ADRs (dependency-free domain, SQLite source of truth, deterministic FSM, ports and adapters, single transaction boundary, hybrid plugin core, Cline file-channel worker) and 5 open risks (architecture drift, SQLite leakage, plugin-core god-object creep, partial JSON in the Cline channel, at-least-once delivery without de-duplication), plus the canonical ArchitectureVersion 1.0 and the project. VERIFICATION: python -m pytest -q -> 895 passed, 0 failed (43 new tests). End-to-end smoke: seed creates 14 records and 19 audit entries; ContextBuilder then returns project=Architecture Lifecycle Assistant, architecture=1.0, 3 rules, 7 accepted ADRs and 5 open risks; the persisted rules equal ARCHITECTURE_V1.rule_ids(); re-seeding creates nothing. Architecture self-check still green: 28 modules, 0 violations, compliant, sqlite3 confined to infrastructure. No refactor of existing code was needed. FORWARD-LOOKING NOTE (not a blocker for this step, therefore not filed as an architecture_question): the Step 4 allowed-import matrix lets no layer except architecture itself import the architecture layer, so a production composition root that must build the canonical ArchitectureVersion from ARCHITECTURE_V1 has no legal home yet; today the composition side is the test suite, which is fine for Step 8, but Step 9 (Orchestrator + Scheduler) will likely need that composition seam and may require an explicit matrix extension at that point. Scope respected: no Orchestrator/Scheduler (Step 9), no AI advisors/judge, no UI, no Database or domain changes, no new migration.
